transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

I'm here because... well, it's probably just me being overly sensitive, but I've been having a bit of a hard time lately. I'm an artist, and recently I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt. And, um... I just kept getting these really uncomfortable, unwanted thoughts while I was putting it together. 

It sounds silly to say out loud, but I kept thinking that if I made one wrong color choice, or if a photo placement was just slightly off, it meant I was going to dishonor her somehow... or that it proved I didn't actually love her enough. I tried to just brush them off as normal creative doubts—because artists get those all the time, right?—but I just couldn't seem to shake them this time. Does that... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you usually help people with?
Did you feel a strong need to repeat certain actions or check things multiple times while working on the memorial piece?

Well, um... maybe a little bit? I mean, I think most artists are a bit perfectionistic, right? It's good to be thorough. But... yeah, I guess I did do that a bit more than usual. 

I would, um... I'd end up rereading the label text a lot. And I'd keep nudging the same objects on my work table, just moving them a tiny fraction of an inch, and checking the layout photos over and over again. I just had to keep doing it until it finally felt, I don't know, 'settled' in my mind. Even though a part of me completely knows it’s already fine and I’m really just losing valuable studio time. 

That’s probably just a normal part of the creative process when you're stressed, don't you think? I really hope that doesn't sound too strange.
Did these thoughts and behaviors interfere with your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

Um... I wouldn't say it's interfering in a *significant* way. I mean, I'm still getting the vast majority of my work done, and my relationships are fine! I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. 

But... well, I guess the extra time I've been losing in the studio has caused a couple of minor hiccups. I, um... I actually missed a grant deadline recently because I just couldn't get the application materials to feel right. And I ended up backing out of a gallery talk that I was really excited about, just because I felt so behind and overwhelmed. 

But that happens to everyone sometimes, right? Just getting a little behind schedule? I'm sure it's nothing major, but I just wanted to be honest with you. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you experience excessive worry or anxiety in your daily life when you're not working on a specific project?

Um... no, I don't think so? When I'm not in the middle of a big piece, I'm actually pretty relaxed, I think. 

I mean, I have normal everyday worries, like, you know, paying rent or remembering to pick up groceries, but nothing that feels... excessive. I really try to be a positive, easygoing person when I'm just hanging out with friends or doing normal life stuff. So, no, it's really just when I'm working on something important that I get stuck like that. 

Is that... is that helpful? I hope I'm explaining things clearly enough for you.
Do you ever feel the need to perform specific rituals or routines when you're not working on a project?

Um, no... no, I don't think so. I really don't do anything like that when I'm just living my normal life. 

Like I said, I'm pretty relaxed outside of the studio. I just, you know, get up, have my coffee, go for a walk... just regular, normal things. I don't have any special routines I have to do before leaving the house or anything like that. It's really only when I'm trying to make sure a piece is absolutely perfect that I get a little... caught up in things. 

So, no, nothing like that at all! Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you have unwanted, intrusive thoughts when you're not working on a project?

Um... no, not really. I don't get those kinds of thoughts. 

When I'm away from my art, my mind is pretty quiet, honestly. I might think about what I'm going to make for dinner or, you know, what movie I want to watch, but nothing weird or upsetting just pops into my head out of nowhere. I'm really just a normal, happy person when I'm not stressing over a piece! 

I really hope I'm not sounding like I'm hiding anything... I just genuinely don't have those kinds of thoughts outside of work. Is that okay? Am I giving you the information you need?
Do you think the unwanted thoughts you've been having are only about your art, or can they be about other things as well?

Um, well, like I was saying, it's really just the art. I don't... I don't think they're about anything else. 

When I'm working on a piece, I just get these thoughts that it's wrong, or unbalanced, or that I've ruined it somehow if I don't fix it right that second. But it's just because I care so much about my work, you know? It's not like I have weird thoughts about... I don't know, other people or bad things happening. It's strictly just me wanting my art to be good. 

I mean, that's fairly normal for an artist, right? To be a little obsessive about the work? I just want to make sure you understand that it's really contained to just my studio time. I'm not, like, a mess in the rest of my life or anything! Is that... does that answer your question?
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts about your art are coming from yourself, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of you?

Um, oh, they're definitely from me. It's just my own brain, you know? 

It's not like I'm hearing voices or feeling like someone else is putting thoughts in my head. Nothing scary or... or crazy like that. It's just me being a perfectionist, getting in my own way because I want the colors or the symmetry to be exactly right. It's just my own inner critic being a little too loud sometimes. 

That's an important distinction, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm being clear that it's just my own normal thoughts, just... focused a bit too hard on my work. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for?
How much distress do these unwanted thoughts and behaviors cause you when they happen?

Um, it's... it's not too bad, honestly. I mean, it's a little frustrating sometimes, but I'm still getting most of my work done. It's not like I'm completely paralyzed or anything! 

I guess... well, the extra time I end up spending in the studio, just making sure everything is perfect, it did kind of make me miss a grant deadline recently. And I, um, I actually backed out of a gallery talk I really wanted to do, just because I felt like I needed to stay in the studio and fix a piece instead. 

But I mean, artists are supposed to be dedicated, right? It's just a little bump in the road. It doesn't mean I'm falling apart or anything. I'm still functioning fine overall. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I just want to be honest with you.
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts about your art are something you want to have, or do they feel alien or unwelcome to you?

Um... well, I definitely don't *want* to have them. They're... they are pretty unwelcome. I mean, usually I just try to use my perfectionism as motivation, but... well, to be completely honest, the reason I actually made this appointment was because of something that happened recently. 

I was, um, working on a memorial piece for my aunt. And I just kept getting these really... awful, unwanted thoughts. It wasn't like my usual artistic process at all. I kept having this intense feeling that I was going to dishonor her somehow? Like... like if I made one wrong photo placement, or if I chose the wrong color, it would mean that I didn't love her enough. 

And I just... I couldn't brush them off like my normal creative doubts. They just stuck there, and it felt really terrible. But, um, grief can make people think weird things, right? I hope I'm explaining this okay... I just don't want you to think I'm completely losing my grip on reality or anything. Am I making sense?
Would you say that these unwanted thoughts and the extra time you spend in the studio are causing you a lot of distress?

Um, well, like I was mentioning a little bit ago... I really don't want to make it sound like a huge crisis, because I am still getting most of my work done. I promise I'm usually very reliable! 

But... I guess, yeah, if I'm being completely honest, it is causing some distress. Just because... well, as I said, the extra time I end up losing in the studio already cost me that grant deadline. And having to back out of the gallery talk that I had actually really wanted to do... that was pretty upsetting for me. I was really looking forward to it. 

But I mean, I'm still managing things overall, you know? It's just a few missed opportunities. I hope that answers your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been experiencing these unwanted thoughts and behaviors when working on your art?

Um, gosh... I'm actually not entirely sure? I hope it's okay that I don't have an exact timeline for you. I'm sorry if that's not very helpful... I guess I just haven't really been keeping track. 

It feels like I've always been a little particular about my work, you know, just wanting it to be good. But these specific, really unwanted thoughts... they sort of just crept up on me recently. I didn't really notice exactly when it crossed over from just normal artist perfectionism into something else. 

Is that an okay answer? I feel bad I can't give you a better estimate... I just really didn't realize it was becoming a pattern until I was working on that memorial piece.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family due to the time you spend on your art or the distress it causes you?

Um... no, I don't think so? I really try hard to not let my work affect my relationships. I mean, my friends and family are incredibly supportive, and I always make sure to text people back and be there for them. 

I would feel just awful if my... if my extra studio time made anyone feel neglected. So, no, no big problems or arguments or anything like that. Maybe I've been a little less social lately just because I've been so focused, but they understand. I always try to be a good friend, I promise. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just really wouldn't want you to think I'm ignoring the people I care about. Is that helpful at all?
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts about your art are a part of who you are, or do they feel like they're not really coming from you?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I'm honestly not entirely sure? I hope it's okay that I don't have a very clear answer for that. 

I mean, I've always prided myself on being really dedicated to my art, so wanting things to be exactly right definitely feels like *me*. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, like, losing touch with reality or anything! It's definitely just my own brain. It's just that lately, those thoughts get a little... stuck, I guess? 

But I think they're still coming from me, just... me trying a bit too hard to do a good job? I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm not explaining this very well, and I really want to give you the right information. Does that make sense at all?
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts about your art are in line with your own values and beliefs, or do they feel like they're contradicting them?

Um... wow, that's another really good question. I... I'm actually not sure how to answer that one either. I hope that's alright? 

I guess... I mean, I value doing good work, you know? Being a good artist and putting out things that are beautiful and meaningful. So wanting it to be perfect, that definitely aligns with what I believe in. I really care about my art. 

But the... the part where I get so stuck that I can't even finish a piece, or where I feel like if I don't fix one tiny brushstroke then the whole thing is ruined... I don't know if that's a value? It just feels like I'm trying to be responsible and do my best, and maybe just going a tiny bit overboard. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm just talking in circles. I don't think they're contradicting my beliefs, necessarily, just... maybe an exaggerated version of them? Is that a normal way to feel? I really hope I'm giving you the kind of answers you need...
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts about your art are something that you would normally think, or do they feel foreign to you?

Um... I think they're things I would normally think? Just, you know, because I'm so passionate about my work. I wouldn't say they feel foreign or strange, really. 

Like, it's totally normal for an artist to want to get the colors exactly right, or to fix a line that's a little wobbly. So the thoughts themselves are just... me being me. Just me wanting to be a good artist. I wouldn't want you to think I'm having bizarre thoughts or anything! 

It's just that maybe I think them a little more often than I used to? But they definitely feel like my own normal thoughts. I hope that makes sense? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful. Did that answer what you were asking?
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts about your art are something that you would normally think and agree with, or do they feel like they are contradicting your own beliefs and values?

Oh, gosh... I feel like I might be repeating myself, which probably means I didn't do a very good job explaining it just a minute ago. I'm really sorry about that! 

Um... I definitely agree with the core of the thoughts. Like, wanting to create something beautiful and accurate is very much in line with my values as an artist, so I wouldn't say they contradict my beliefs at all. I definitely agree with wanting to do good work. 

It's really just... the intensity of it, maybe? Like, I normally think these things, but lately I just get a little carried away trying to make sure everything is perfect. I really hope that's a better answer for you? Please let me know if I'm still not quite hitting what you're looking for, I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you ever have unwanted, intrusive thoughts or feel the need to perform specific rituals when you're not thinking about your art?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. It's really just focused on my artwork. 

When I'm not in my studio or, you know, working on a piece, I don't really have any thoughts like that. And I definitely don't do any... well, rituals or anything. I'm pretty much just completely normal outside of my art. 

I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means it's not too serious, right? I really wouldn't want you to think I'm struggling all the time or doing strange things around the house. It really is just because I care so much about my work. Does that help? I can try to think harder if you need me to, but I'm pretty sure it's just the art.
Have you ever felt like you couldn't control these unwanted thoughts about your art, even when you tried to stop thinking about them?

Um... well, I usually try really hard to just push through them. I don't want to make it sound like I'm totally out of control or anything! But... I guess recently, there was a time when I really couldn't stop them, which is actually why I decided to come in. 

I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt, and... I hope this doesn't sound terrible, but I just kept getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. Like, my brain was telling me that one wrong photo placement, or, you know, a slightly wrong color choice would mean I didn't love her enough. 

I really tried to just stop thinking about it and brush them off like my normal creative doubts—because usually I can do that!—but I just couldn't. I couldn't turn it off. I know that sounds a little intense... I really hope you don't think badly of me for having thoughts like that. I know it's silly. Does that answer what you were asking?
Have you ever experienced any significant distress or impairment in your daily life due to these unwanted thoughts or behaviors related to your art?

Um... I wouldn't say it's, like, severe impairment or anything like that. I'm really trying hard to keep everything on track, and I am still getting most of my work done. I promise I'm not just sitting around doing nothing! 

But... well, I guess the extra time I've been losing in the studio trying to get things just right... it did kind of cause a little hiccup recently. I actually missed a deadline for a grant application because I was so caught up in fixing a piece. And, um, I also ended up backing out of a gallery talk that I really, really wanted to do, just because I was so stressed about my work not being ready. 

I feel so silly even admitting that, because I know I should be able to manage my time better. I really don't want you to think I'm irresponsible or that I'm falling apart, because I'm usually very reliable! It's just been a little harder lately. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
